sources.title: [bf1942] RE : [bf1942] admin.remote - icculus BF1942 Linux server mailing list
[bf1942] Admin commands not working on latest version? ("Use 4711 for the remote console")
LANCommander.Servers.Battlefield1942 - compose maps 4711:4711/tcp with the comment "RCON"
All strings found in IDA - BF1942 retail binary string dump

notes: No Source RCON. BF1942's remote channel is its own remote console: admin.enableRemoteConsole <username> <password> [port], default TCP 4711, with an operator connecting via RemoteConsole.exe in the server's AdminTool folder; the wire protocol is proprietary and undocumented, hence flavour "custom". Port 4711 is two-sourced (icculus list 000683, "Use 4711 for the remote console ... 4711 is the default port", and the LANCommander container mapping 4711:4711/tcp # RCON). Username and password are arguments of that one command, not named settings, so portSetting/passwordSetting are null. CORRECTION (review 2026-09-13): an earlier draft justified transport by claiming the icculus list says admin commands cannot be run in the dedicated server's own console window. That is backwards. Message 000788 says the opposite: "When you are sitting in front of your server/console (i.e. NOT remote), then you just issue the admin command right into the console (i.e. game.listplayers and admin.kickplayer <number>)", reached by pressing the ` key to take the console out of status-display mode. The "you cannot run commands there" quote is from a different thread (000683) and refers to the startup window where a launch error is printed, not to the in-server console. The server therefore DOES accept these commands locally; transport is recorded as rcon because the remote console is the channel a remote runtime can actually drive, not because a local console channel is impossible. Argument-form disagreement on the enable command: the icculus FAQ and the MoonGamers list give admin.enableRemoteConsole [username] [password] [#port]; LANCommander and the KenZoe FAQ present it as a 0/1 toggle (admin.enableRemoteConsole 1). Probe both forms. Command casing comes from the strings in the retail binary (kickPlayer, kickPlayerByName, banPlayer, banPlayerKey, listPlayers, serverMessage, sayAll, setServerWelcomeMessage, listBannedAddresses, removeAddressFromBanList, enableRemoteConsole); community lists (MoonGamers, TweakGuides, Gamesclan) misspell listBannedAddresses as "listBannedAdresses". Source coverage is NOT uniform across the four commands: kick, ban and listPlayers appear in the binary dump, MoonGamers, the KenZoe FAQ and LANCommander; admin.serverMessage appears in the binary dump, the KenZoe FAQ ("message = admin.servermessage", yellow server text) and LANCommander, but NOT in the MoonGamers list; game.setServerWelcomeMessage appears in the binary dump, LANCommander and the XGamingServer reference serversettings.con (which literally contains game.setServerWelcomeMessage 0 ""), but NOT in MoonGamers or the KenZoe FAQ. Every recorded command still clears two independent sources, so confidence stays high. The moderation id is the per-session numeric player id printed by game.listPlayers - not a name, CD-key hash or account id; admin.kickPlayerByName <name> also exists but has no ban equivalent, so the numeric id is recorded. Disagreement: LANCommander documents an optional timeout on ban (admin.banplayer <id> [timeout]); no other source shows it, so {duration} is not used and the ban is recorded as permanent. game.sayAll exists (binary dump, MoonGamers) and is global chat; admin.serverMessage is the server-side yellow broadcast and is used for say. UNVERIFIED: the literal text layout of game.listPlayers output could not be sourced anywhere. LANCommander says it prints ids, names and CD-key hashes, so playerParse.linePattern has been widened to accept both a bare leading numeric id and an "Id:"-prefixed form, and the name group may swallow a trailing key hash. This regex is a guess and must be confirmed against a live server before anyone relies on the roster. Bans are stored as IP addresses and CD-key hashes, so there is no unban taking a session player id - unban is expressed as banList.liveUnban (admin.removeAddressFromBanList <ip>), and the substituted {playerId} there is the IP captured by lineIdPattern, not a session id. The banlist.con path is single-sourced (LANCommander). Enabling the remote console was reported in 2002 to cause an "ASE" hang on map change.
